desc:
Shipping rates, zones and delivery options setup makes the prices at checkout match what delivery really costs you. Ecom Swift LLC builds your zones, rates and rules in your own store and tests each one with sample orders.

## What are shipping rules?

Shipping rules are the settings that decide which delivery choices a shopper sees and what each one costs. They depend on where the parcel goes, how heavy it is, what it contains and what the order is worth. They also cover free shipping thresholds, local pickup and local delivery.

The rules sit in your store settings, often grouped by shipping profile and zone. Small mistakes in them are easy to miss, because a rule rarely breaks loudly. It just charges the wrong amount.

## Why wrong shipping prices cost you twice

If the rate is too low, you pay the difference from your margin on every order. If it is too high, shoppers see an unpleasant surprise at checkout and leave. Both errors are quiet, and both repeat on every order until someone notices.

Confusing options cause a third problem. When shoppers see four unclear choices, or none that fit, they hesitate. Clear names and sensible defaults make the decision easy.

## How shipping setup affects conversion and margin

Shipping is one of the most common reasons a cart is abandoned, because extra costs appear late. Showing a fair, understandable price, and a free shipping threshold where it makes sense, helps shoppers plan their basket. A threshold can also encourage a larger order.

On the cost side, rules based on weight, size and destination keep your price close to what the carrier charges. A margin check against real carrier costs shows which zones lose money, so you can adjust before the loss grows.

## What a well-built shipping setup includes

- Zones by country or region, with the correct countries in each.
- Flat, weight-based and price-based rates where they fit.
- A free shipping threshold, if it suits your margins.
- Standard and express delivery choices with clear names.
- Local pickup or local delivery, if you offer them.
- Separate profiles for bulky, fragile or small goods.
- Live carrier rates where your plan supports them.
- A duties and taxes message for export orders.
- A margin check against your carrier costs.
- A rule sheet that lists every setting in plain words.

## What we do

We begin with your carrier price lists, product weights and the countries you sell to. We design a rule set that fits, then enter it in your store's shipping settings. We group products into profiles so each product group gets the right rates.

Then we test. We place sample orders for each zone and product group and check the price at checkout against what we expected. Anything that does not match is corrected and tested again. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in the number of zones and in advanced features, from core rates to delivery options, product rules, live rates and international messages.

We recommend rates based on your costs, but you decide the prices. You receive the rule sheet and handover notes, so you can change rules later with confidence.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Base rates on real carrier invoices and packed weights.
- Use plain names such as Standard delivery and Express delivery.
- Set a threshold that keeps the average order profitable.
- Review the rules when carrier prices change.
- Test a checkout in each zone after any edit.

**Avoid:**
- Offering free shipping to every country without checking costs.
- Leaving products in the default profile when they differ in size.
- Hiding the shipping cost until the last step.
- Changing rates without a test order.
- Copying a competitor's prices instead of your own costs.

## Who this is for

This suits a store opening to new countries and unsure how to price each one. It suits an owner who suspects that shipping charges lose money on heavy goods. It also suits a business that wants to add local pickup or delivery alongside parcel shipping.

## What we need from you

Send your carrier rate cards or invoices, your list of destinations and your product weights. We also need a collaborator or staff user with access to shipping settings. We do not ask for passwords. We reply with a short plan, show you the proposed rules and apply them after your approval.
